title: Fundamental Duty to Protect Environment — Article 51A(g) in PIL

content.overview: Article 51A(g) states the citizen’s fundamental duty to protect and improve the natural environment. In PIL it orients environmental claims alongside Article 21 and Article 48A, but it is not ordinarily treated as an independently enforceable right like Part III guarantees.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Environmental public injury? (2) Art 21 and/or 48A also pleaded? (3) Role of 51A(g) as duty/orientation? (4) Standing bona fides? (5) Forum 32/226?
content.study:
Core frame: Article 51A(g) is a Fundamental Duty. Courts may use it to interpret environmental obligations and to support the policy context of environmental PIL. Primary enforceable hooks typically remain Article 21 (life/dignity) and statutory duties, enforced through Articles 32 and 226.

Use in argument: Cite 51A(g) to show constitutional concern for environmental protection and citizen responsibility; do not treat it alone as a free-standing cause of action without a justiciable rights or duty frame.

Current-law framing: Articles 51A(g), 21, 48A, 32, 226. Case-law verification remains separate.

sections.heading: Text and character of Article 51A(g)
sections.body: Duty of every citizen to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.

sections.heading: Duty vs enforceable right
sections.body: Fundamental Duties guide and orient; Part III rights and statutory duties more often supply the enforceable base for writ relief.

sections.heading: Link to Articles 21 and 48A
sections.body: Environmental PIL commonly pairs 51A(g) with Article 21 (life/dignity) and Article 48A (State duty).

sections.heading: Standing and forum
sections.body: Bona fide public-interest petitioners may seek environmental enforcement under 32/226 where injury is public and justiciable.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body: 51A(g) citation does not validate private boundary disputes or vague omnibus prayers.

examples.title: River pollution PIL
examples.body: Community petition cites Arts 21, 48A and 51A(g) against untreated discharge affecting public water use.

hypotheticals.question: Is Article 51A(g) alone enough for a writ?
hypotheticals.analysis: Usually pair with Article 21 or a statutory/public duty framed under 32/226; 51A(g) orients rather than standing alone as a complete cause of action.

misconceptions.trap: 51A(g) creates a personal enforceable right identical to Article 21.
misconceptions.correction: It is a Fundamental Duty; enforceability runs mainly through rights and statutory duties via writ jurisdiction.

cases.name: Bandhua Mukti Morcha v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Flexible procedure for effective rights enforcement.
cases.relevance: Process model for structural claims; verification open.

cases.name: S.P. Gupta v. Union of India
cases.ratioDecidendi: Standing may be relaxed for bona fide public redress.

cases.name: State of Uttaranchal v. Balwant Singh Chaufal
cases.ratioDecidendi: Credentials, motive, public injury, no personal gain.
